lines: Bluey found a warm blanket near the backyard grass and thought it looked like fun.
Bluey turned the pillow over to the cool side and sighed.
Bluey set the warm blanket where it would be handy, then stretched out.
Bluey let the busy day melt away and got completely comfy.
Bluey shook out the pillow and punched it into shape.
The clock in the hall ticked on, patient and slow.
The sky had that deep, velvety look it gets at night.
Bluey heard a tiny sniffle from across the room.
Bingo needed someone to sit with them.
Bluey promised they would not go far.
Bluey fetched the warm blanket and brought it over to Bingo.
Bluey tucked the edges in and smoothed everything flat.
They rearranged the pillows until it felt comfortable.
They tried again with the light left gently on.
Bingo drifted off knowing they were looked after.
Bingo was safe and snug and warm at last.
The little problem had completely gone away.
The night hummed a slow, steady tune they could feel.
Nothing moved now except the gentle moon.
Nothing stirred except the curtain and the clock.
And that is where the night left them: safe, warm, asleep.
Bluey sank down into the deepest kind of sleepy.
Bluey and Bingo slept on, dreaming happily of the fun.

lines: Bluey found a night light near the backyard grass and thought it looked like fun.
Bluey propped the pillow behind and sank down happily.
Bluey rubbed tired eyes and looked around the quiet backyard grass.
Bluey stacked the pillows neatly and gave them a pat.
Bluey whispered goodnight to the toys on the shelf.
The curtains were open just enough for the moonlight.
The garden gate swung once and settled back with a click.
Bluey heard a small, uncertain voice coming from the backyard grass.
Muffin was still wide awake when the moon was up.
Bluey put a gentle arm around Muffin and smiled.
They made a cosy cave out of pillows and quilts.
They tried again with the light left gently on.
Together they found the best place, then made it soft and warm.
They rearranged the pillows until it felt comfortable.
The worrying feeling drifted off somewhere else.
The room felt softer once the problem was solved.
Muffin whispered thank you and closed their eyes.
The night lay over the whole house like a quilt.
The little lamp was turned down to the gentlest glow.
The dark was soft, like a room with the lights down low.
Nothing worried them, and nothing woke them.
The house kept them safe while they slept.
Bluey and Muffin slept on, dreaming happily of the fun.

lines: Bluey found a bedtime storybook near the backyard grass and thought it looked like fun.
Bluey laid out the slippers side by side and stepped in.
Bluey rolled over once, then found the very best spot.
Bluey slid under the covers and wriggled the cold away.
Bluey straightened the quilt and smoothed it down flat.
All the little lights in the street had gone out.
Everything outdoors had gone soft and grey and sleepy.
Bandit was tired, but sleep would not come.
Bluey noticed Bandit blinking at the ceiling.
Bluey decided to help Bandit straight away.
Bluey sat with Bandit until the wriggling stopped.
They looked around the backyard grass very carefully and very slowly.
Bluey tucked the bedtime storybook around Bandit very carefully.
They whispered about lovely things until it felt calmer.
Bluey felt glad, and warm, and ready for bed.
The worrying feeling drifted off somewhere else.
Bluey was glad they had got up to help.
The quilt was warm and the pillow was soft.
Nothing needed doing, and nothing needed saying.
Somewhere a clock ticked slowly, on and on.
And there they stayed, asleep and warm, until morning.
The house kept them safe while they slept.
Bluey and Bandit slept on, dreaming happily of the fun.

<LINE>Bluey found a night light near the bedroom window and thought it looked like fun.</LINE>
<LINE>Bluey rolled over once, then found the very best spot.</LINE>
<LINE>Bluey set the night light where it would be handy, then stretched out.</LINE>
<LINE>Bluey pulled the quilt up to the chin and sighed happily.</LINE>
<LINE>Bluey let the busy day melt away and got completely comfy.</LINE>
<LINE>The garden gate swung once and settled back with a click.</LINE>
<LINE>The neighbourhood had gone quiet, house by house.</LINE>
<LINE>It was very dark by the bedroom window in the middle of the night.</LINE>
<LINE>A little shadow moved slowly across the dark bedroom window.</LINE>
<LINE>Bluey whispered a plan and Bandit nodded slowly.</LINE>
<LINE>Bluey counted three and walked forward bravely.</LINE>
<LINE>Bluey checked the hallway twice and felt quite brave.</LINE>
<LINE>They listened hard and heard only the wind.</LINE>
<LINE>They checked the whole bedroom window and found nothing scary.</LINE>
<LINE>Bluey felt calm, and rather pleased.</LINE>
<LINE>The hallway felt just like any other room.</LINE>
<LINE>Bandit let out a happy little breath at last.</LINE>
<LINE>The night wrapped the house up, warm and quiet.</LINE>
<LINE>Every single sound settled down and went to sleep.</LINE>
<LINE>The little lamp was turned down to the gentlest glow.</LINE>
<LINE>Sleep wrapped round the room and would not let go.</LINE>
<LINE>The whole room felt heavy and warm and still.</LINE>
<LINE>Bluey and Bandit slept on, dreaming happily of the fun.</LINE>
<END>

lines: Bluey found a bedtime storybook near the bedroom window and thought it looked like fun.
Bluey tucked the teddy under one arm and got comfortable.
Bluey rubbed tired eyes and looked around the quiet bedroom window.
Bluey let the busy day melt away and got completely comfy.
Bluey wrapped up snugly and grinned at how soft the bedtime storybook was.
All the little lights in the street had gone out.
A sleepy breeze wandered past the bedroom window.
A little shadow moved slowly across the dark bedroom window.
The shadows on the wall looked taller than usual.
Bluey offered to stay up a little longer.
They found the noise was only a curtain flapping.
Bluey counted three and walked forward bravely.
Bluey crept past the creaky floorboard and waved.
Bluey took one more step and was not worried.
They were not afraid of anything in the dark.
The hallway felt just like any other room.
Bluey felt proud, and very ready for sleep.
The world outside had gone completely still.
The quilt was warm and the pillow was soft.
Everything was still, and everything was well.
The night held them gently, the way a quilt does.
The two friends slept on, warm and safe and calm.
Bluey and Bingo slept on, dreaming happily of the fun.

lines: Bluey found a soft teddy near the bedroom window and thought it looked like fun.
Bluey put away the day and hung up the busy thoughts.
Bluey plumped the pillow twice and pulled up the sheet.
Bluey put the slippers by the bed and climbed under the quilt.
Bluey rubbed tired eyes and looked around the quiet bedroom window.
A thin cloud slid across the moon and made the room dim.
Outside the window the sky had turned lovely and dark.
The shadows on the wall looked taller than usual.
Muffin was wide awake by the dark bedroom window at night.
Bluey offered to sit there as long as it took.
They found the noise was only a curtain flapping.
At the last step, the shadow was only a pile of clothes.
Muffin kept close and held on tight.
They listened hard and heard only the wind.
There was nothing left to be scared of now.
The night felt small and safe and friendly.
The house was quiet, and nothing was frightening.
The little lamp was turned down to the gentlest glow.
The curtains breathed in and out very slowly.
The house settled into its quiet, sleepy self.
They slept the way tired children do: deeply and quietly.
Muffin fell asleep with a tiny, contented smile.
Bluey and Muffin slept on, dreaming happily of the fun.

lines: Bluey found a woolly quilt near the bedroom window and thought it looked like fun.
Bluey drank the last of the warm milk and yawned.
Bluey pulled the quilt up to the chin and sighed happily.
Bluey whispered goodnight to the moon through the glass.
Bluey stacked the pillows neatly and gave them a pat.
A cool breeze tapped the window once, and then wandered off.
The night was cool and still, and everything sounded small and far away.
Bluey felt a small flutter in the tummy but stayed still.
Bandit did not like the long walk in the dark.
Bluey offered to sit there as long as it took.
Bluey crept past the creaky floorboard and waved.
They checked the whole bedroom window and found nothing scary.
At the last step, the shadow was only a pile of clothes.
They walked the hallway slowly and found it ordinary.
Brave feelings lasted all the way back to bed.
Bandit let out a happy little breath at last.
Bluey felt proud, and very ready for sleep.
The house breathed out and settled for the night.
The night wrapped the house up, warm and quiet.
Everything was tidy and calm and gently dim.
Bluey was fast asleep before the quilt was even settled.
Bluey snuggled down deep and let sleep take over.
Bluey and Bandit slept on, dreaming happily of the fun.

lines: Bluey found a warm blanket near the bedroom window and thought it looked like fun.
Bluey propped the pillow behind and sank down happily.
Bluey folded the covers just so and made everything nice and neat.
Bluey shooed the last thoughts away and closed the curtains.
Bluey plumped the pillow twice and pulled up the sheet.
A little moon lamp glowed in the corner of the quiet room.
A thin cloud slid across the moon and made the room dim.
The story would not end the way Bluey had planned.
The blanket slid off every single time.
Bluey asked if a story might help.
With a bit of patience, it started to work.
It took three goes, and then it worked.
Bluey tried a different way and it almost worked.
Bluey wiggled it gently until it sat just right.
It stayed, and it worked, and that was enough.
Bluey felt satisfied and ready for sleep.
It was done, and it was finally time to rest.
It was the quietest part of the whole night.
The night wrapped the house up, warm and quiet.
The dark was soft, like a room with the lights down low.
And that was the end: one more sleepy, happy night.
Bingo mumbled something happy and slept on.
Bluey and Bingo slept on, dreaming happily of the fun.

lines: Bluey found a night light near the bedroom window and thought it looked like fun.
Bluey whispered goodnight to the toys on the shelf.
Bluey set the night light where it would be handy, then stretched out.
Bluey rubbed tired eyes and looked around the quiet bedroom window.
Bluey kicked off the slippers and wiggled ten tired toes.
A soft hush fell over the street and the roofs.
A plane blinked quietly across the top of the sky.
The covers kept slipping off the bed in a silly way.
Bluey could not find the best way to help, and that was that.
Bluey told Muffin they were not on their own.
Bluey did not rush it and did not give up.
Bluey thought about it again and tried once more.
Slow and steady really did make it all work.
They changed one small thing and gave it another go.
The little problem turned out to be no trouble at all.
It stayed put, right where it should be.
All that trying was the sleepiest part of the day.
Everything had that safe, tucked-in feeling.
The last little sound faded out into the dark.
The pillows settled, and the quilt settled, and the room settled.
Muffin slept on, breathing softly by the bedroom window.
And every star watched over them until morning.
Bluey and Muffin slept on, dreaming happily of the fun.

Bluey slid under the covers and wriggled the cold away.
Bluey shooed the last thoughts away and closed the curtains.
Bluey pulled the quilt up to the chin and sighed happily.
Bluey yawned twice, stretched long, and settled right down.
One star seemed to blink, as if it was getting sleepy too.
The night was cool and still, and everything sounded small and far away.
The story would not end the way Bluey had planned.
Bluey could not settle while something felt unfinished.
Bluey said two kind words and meant every one.
Bluey wiggled it gently until it sat just right.
It was not perfect the second time, but it was better.
Bluey steadied it carefully and tried one last time.
Bluey did not rush it and did not give up.

Bluey was pleased with their careful work.
It worked at last, and that was that.

Everything was tidy and calm and gently dim.
The lamp went dark and the room went softer still.
Morning was a long, long way off yet.
And so the long, soft night began.
Bluey and Bandit slept on, dreaming happily of the fun.

lines: Bluey found a soft teddy near the bedroom window and thought it looked like fun.
Bluey propped the pillow behind and sank down happily.
Bluey drank some water, then lay down for the night.
Bluey rubbed tired eyes and looked around the quiet bedroom window.
Bluey put on soft pyjamas and sat down near the bedroom window.
Everything outdoors had gone soft and grey and sleepy.
A thin cloud slid across the moon and made the room dim.
The bedtime song would not come out quite right.
Bluey could not find the best way to help, and that was that.
Bluey offered a hand and a warm smile.
Bluey steadied it carefully and tried one last time.
Bluey took a breath and tried again, more slowly this time.
They took a short rest, then tried the whole thing again.
It took three goes, and then it worked.
All the effort had been worth it.
It worked at last, and that was that.
Bluey was pleased with their careful work.
Everything had that safe, tucked-in feeling.
The house creaked once, the way houses do at night.
The last light clicked off and the room went soft.
And that was the end: one more sleepy, happy night.
The whole room felt heavy and warm and still.
Bluey and Bingo slept on, dreaming happily of the fun.

<LINE>Bluey found a bedtime storybook near the cubby cushion and thought it looked like fun.</LINE>
<LINE>Bluey straightened the quilt and smoothed it down flat.</LINE>
<LINE>Bluey tucked the quilt in at the sides and yawned.</LINE>
<LINE>Bluey rubbed tired eyes and looked around the quiet cubby cushion.</LINE>
<LINE>Bluey turned the pillow over to the cool side and sighed.</LINE>
<LINE>A plane blinked quietly across the top of the sky.</LINE>
<LINE>The curtains were open just enough for the moonlight.</LINE>
<LINE>Bandit had nothing at all to snuggle under.</LINE>
<LINE>Bandit had nothing cosy to keep them warm.</LINE>
<LINE>Bluey said they would figure it out, step by step.</LINE>
<LINE>Two friends, one blanket, and plenty of space for both.</LINE>
<LINE>Both of them squeezed in and made it work.</LINE>
<LINE>They huddled up together and told jokes softly.</LINE>
<LINE>They made a warm pocket for four cold feet.</LINE>
<LINE>They settled down together, cosy and content.</LINE>
<LINE>Neither of them was cold any more.</LINE>
<LINE>Nobody minded sharing, and nobody was cold.</LINE>
<LINE>It was the quietest part of the whole night.</LINE>
<LINE>Their eyelids grew heavy, and their arms felt warm and relaxed.</LINE>
<LINE>The moon kept a soft, silver watch through the window.</LINE>
<LINE>The room breathed slowly in and out all night.</LINE>
<LINE>They slept the way tired children do: deeply and quietly.</LINE>
<LINE>Bluey and Bandit slept on, dreaming happily of the fun.</LINE>
<END>

lines: Bluey found a soft teddy near the cubby cushion and thought it looked like fun.
Bluey shook out the pillow and punched it into shape.
Bluey folded the covers just so and made everything nice and neat.
Bluey whispered goodnight to the moon through the glass.
Bluey drank the last of the warm milk and yawned.
The moon was so round and bright that it lit up the whole room.
The night was cool and still, and everything sounded small and far away.
Bingo had a chilly bed and nothing warm to hold.
Bingo wanted a turn with the only warm thing.
Bluey told Bingo they were doing really well.
Bluey made a nest with room enough for two.
Both of them squeezed in and made it work.
They shared the warm corner and the soft pillow.
Bluey moved over so there was room for both.
Two friends, one quilt, and no cold corners.
The blanket felt warm because it was shared.
Kindness was easy when there was plenty to go round.
It was the kind of quiet that meant a good sleep was coming.
The world outside had gone completely still.
Nothing stirred except the curtain and the clock.
The whole room felt heavy and warm and still.
Bluey was asleep before the counting finished.
Bluey and Bingo slept on, dreaming happily of the fun.

lines: Bluey found a woolly quilt near the cubby cushion and thought it looked like fun.
Bluey fluffed up the pillow and tucked the woolly quilt in tight.
Bluey put away the day and hung up the busy thoughts.
Bluey whispered goodnight to the toys on the shelf.
Bluey tucked the quilt in at the sides and yawned.
The night was cool and still, and everything sounded small and far away.
The curtains moved a little, and the shadows danced quietly.
Bluey saw Muffin hugging their knees in the dark.
There was one cosy spot, and it was already taken.
Bluey said they would stay until Muffin felt better.
Bluey offered half and kept half, which felt fair.
They made room so both of them could lie down.
They agreed to swap halfway through the night.
Bluey wound the music box and shared the quiet tune.
Sharing made the room feel warmer and kinder.
Muffin felt happy and snug again after all.
Muffin beamed and wriggled down happily.
The house settled into its quiet, sleepy self.
The last light clicked off and the room went soft.
It was the kind of quiet that meant a good sleep was coming.
Slowly, quietly, the two of them drifted away.
And that is where the night left them: safe, warm, asleep.
Bluey and Muffin slept on, dreaming happily of the fun.

Bluey tucked the teddy under one arm and got comfortable.

The moonlight lay quietly over the cubby cushion like a silver sheet.
Both of them were cosy, and both were sound asleep.
Their breathing slowed to a soft, steady rhythm.
Bluey and Bandit slept on, dreaming happily of the fun.

Bluey and Bingo slept on, dreaming happily of the fun.

<LINE>The moon was up when Bluey found a woolly quilt near the backyard grass.</LINE>
<LINE>Bluey brushed the crumbs off the sheet and climbed in.</LINE>
<LINE>Bluey made a good nest by the backyard grass with a woolly quilt.</LINE>
<LINE>Bluey let the busy day melt away and got completely comfy.</LINE>
<LINE>Bluey plumped the pillow twice and pulled up the sheet.</LINE>
<LINE>The curtains moved a little, and the shadows danced quietly.</LINE>
<LINE>The neighbourhood had gone quiet, house by house.</LINE>
<LINE>Muffin had nothing at all to snuggle under.</LINE>
<LINE>Bluey saw Muffin shivering a little in the dark.</LINE>
<LINE>Bluey said they would sort it out together.</LINE>
<LINE>Bluey said they would take turns with the warmest spot.</LINE>
<LINE>Bluey offered the best spot to Muffin first.</LINE>
<LINE>They wrapped up together and shared the warm spot.</LINE>
<LINE>They made a warm pocket for four cold feet.</LINE>
<LINE>Two friends, one quilt, and no cold corners.</LINE>
<LINE>Muffin said they would share next time too.</LINE>
<LINE>They both felt warm, and very, very sleepy.</LINE>
<LINE>It was the kind of quiet that meant a good sleep was coming.</LINE>
<LINE>The world outside had gone completely still.</LINE>
<LINE>The quilt was warm and the pillow was soft.</LINE>
<LINE>The two friends slept on, warm and safe and calm.</LINE>
<LINE>Everything went soft and slow, and everyone was asleep.</LINE>
<LINE>Bluey and Muffin slept on, cosy and warm and ready for tomorrow.</LINE>
<END>

lines: The moon was up when Bluey found a cosy dressing gown near the backyard grass.
Bluey put on soft pyjamas and sat down near the backyard grass.
Bluey yawned twice, stretched long, and settled right down.
Bluey straightened the quilt and smoothed it down flat.
Bluey drank some water, then lay down for the night.
The curtains moved a little, and the shadows danced quietly.
One star seemed to blink, as if it was getting sleepy too.
Bluey saw Bandit shivering a little in the dark.
Bluey saw that Bandit looked wide awake and worried.
Bluey whispered that it would work out, and meant it.
Both of them squeezed in and made it work.
They agreed to swap halfway through the night.
They decided to share the quilt and the pillow both.
They shared the warm corner and the soft pillow.
The blanket felt warm because it was shared.
They both felt warm, and very, very sleepy.
Nobody minded sharing, and nobody was cold.
Everything was still, and everything was well.
Every single sound settled down and went to sleep.
The dark wrapped around the quiet room like something warm.
They slept the way tired children do: deeply and quietly.
Bluey slept deeply, all the way until morning.
Bluey and Bandit slept on, cosy and warm and ready for tomorrow.

lines: The moon was up when Bluey found a sleepy lullaby near the backyard grass.
Bluey put on soft pyjamas and sat down near the backyard grass.
Bluey laid out the slippers side by side and stepped in.
Bluey pulled the quilt up to the chin and sighed happily.
Bluey wriggled down under the covers and found the cool patch.
The neighbourhood had gone quiet, house by house.
The clock in the hall ticked on, patient and slow.
One warm thing, two sleepy friends, and a problem.
Bluey saw Bingo hugging their knees in the dark.
Bluey promised to stay close by until things were settled.
They decided to share the quilt and the pillow both.
They shared the warm corner and the soft pillow.
Bluey offered half and kept half, which felt fair.
Bluey tucked Bingo in first, then settled down too.
Sharing made the room feel warmer and kinder.
Two friends, one quilt, and no cold corners.
Two friends shared and nobody was left cold.
The dark wrapped around the quiet room like something warm.
The house settled into its quiet, sleepy self.
The house creaked once, the way houses do at night.
And that is where the night left them: safe, warm, asleep.
They slept the way tired children do: deeply and quietly.
Bluey and Bingo slept on, cosy and warm and ready for tomorrow.

lines: The moon was up when Bluey found a warm blanket near the backyard grass.
Bluey rolled over once, then found the very best spot.
Bluey settled in with the warm blanket close by, feeling ready for bed.
Bluey took a long, slow breath and wiggled into the soft covers.
Bluey rubbed tired eyes and looked around the quiet backyard grass.
The last little birds had tucked themselves in for the night.
One star seemed to blink, as if it was getting sleepy too.
Muffin wanted a turn with the only warm thing.
Muffin had a chilly bed and nothing warm to hold.
Bluey promised they would not go far.
Bluey offered half and kept half, which felt fair.
Bluey shared the warm blanket with Muffin and felt good.
Bluey moved over so there was room for both.
Bluey said they would take turns with the warmest spot.
The blanket felt warm because it was shared.
Sharing it made the whole night feel warmer.
Neither of them was cold any more.
The night lay over the whole house like a quilt.
Every single sound settled down and went to sleep.
The whole room grew slow, and soft, and still.
Sleep wrapped round the room and would not let go.
Both of them were cosy, and both were sound asleep.
Bluey and Muffin slept on, cosy and warm and ready for tomorrow.

lines: The moon was up when Bluey found a night light near the backyard grass.
Bluey drank some water, then lay down for the night.
Bluey shook out the pillow and punched it into shape.
Bluey fluffed up the pillow and tucked the night light in tight.
Bluey folded the covers just so and made everything nice and neat.
The garden was dark, and the gate creaked very gently.
Outside the window the sky had turned lovely and dark.
Bluey saw Bandit shivering a little in the dark.
There was one cosy spot, and it was already taken.
Bluey put a gentle arm around Bandit and smiled.
Bluey shared the night light with Bandit and felt good.
Bluey said they would take turns with the warmest spot.
Two friends, one blanket, and plenty of space for both.
They wrapped up together and shared the warm spot.
The blanket felt warm because it was shared.
Bandit beamed and wriggled down happily.
Sharing it made the whole night feel warmer.
The moonlight lay quietly over the backyard grass like a silver sheet.
The pillows settled, and the quilt settled, and the room settled.
The air smelled faintly of soap and warm blankets.
They slept the way tired children do: deeply and quietly.
And so the long, soft night began.
Bluey and Bandit slept on, cosy and warm and ready for tomorrow.

lines: The moon was up when Bluey found a bedtime storybook near the backyard grass.
Bluey tidied the toys away and put them all to bed.
Bluey let the busy day melt away and got completely comfy.
Bluey tucked the quilt in at the sides and yawned.
Bluey brushed the crumbs off the sheet and climbed in.
A soft hush fell over the street and the roofs.
The clock in the hall ticked on, patient and slow.
There was one cosy spot, and it was already taken.
There was one soft bed, but two sleepy friends who wanted it.
Bluey said the kindest thing they could think of.
Bluey said they would take turns with the warmest spot.
Carefully, they split the cosy thing into two snug halves.
They decided to share the quilt and the pillow both.
Two friends, one blanket, and plenty of space for both.
The blanket felt warm because it was shared.
Sharing it made the whole night feel warmer.
Kindness was easy when there was plenty to go round.
Nothing needed doing, and nothing needed saying.
The house creaked once, the way houses do at night.
The quilt was warm and the pillow was soft.
The house kept them safe while they slept.
And so the long, soft night began.
Bluey and Bingo slept on, cosy and warm and ready for tomorrow.

Bluey whispered goodnight to the moon through the glass.
Bluey fluffed up the pillow and tucked the soft teddy in tight.
Everything outside was resting, from the trees to the stones.
Somewhere in the garden a cricket began its slow song.
There was one quilt, and two friends, and a cold night.
Muffin had nothing cosy to keep them warm.
Bluey told Muffin they were doing really well.
Carefully, they split the cosy thing into two snug halves.
They huddled up together and told jokes softly.
They wrapped up together and shared the warm spot.
Bluey tucked Muffin in first, then settled down too.
Muffin beamed and wriggled down happily.
Two friends shared and nobody was left cold.
Kindness made even the dark room feel friendly.
The curtains breathed in and out very slowly.
The dark wrapped around the quiet room like something warm.
Everything was tidy and calm and gently dim.
Slowly, quietly, the two of them drifted away.
The house kept them safe while they slept.
Bluey and Muffin slept on, cosy and warm and ready for tomorrow.

lines: The moon was up when Bluey found a warm blanket near the backyard grass.
Bluey brushed the crumbs off the sheet and climbed in.
Bluey set the warm blanket where it would be handy, then stretched out.
Bluey tucked the quilt in at the sides and yawned.
Bluey laid out the slippers side by side and stepped in.
Somewhere in the garden a cricket began its slow song.
The sky was wide and calm, like a big dark quilt.
The shadows on the wall looked taller than usual.
Bluey wondered what that noise could possibly be.
Bluey put a gentle arm around Bingo and smiled.
Every shadow turned out to be something ordinary.
Bingo held a hand, and they went on together, step by step.
At the last step, the shadow was only a pile of clothes.
Bluey crept past the creaky floorboard and waved.
The house was quiet, and nothing was frightening.
They felt bigger and braver than before.
Bingo felt brave too, and very sleepy.
The house settled into its quiet, sleepy self.
The night hummed a slow, steady tune they could feel.
Everything was tidy and calm and gently dim.
Bluey snuggled down deep and let sleep take over.
Bluey closed their eyes and floated off gently to sleep.
Bluey and Bingo slept on, cosy and warm and ready for tomorrow.

lines: The moon was up when Bluey found a night light near the backyard grass.

The moon kept a soft, silver watch through the window.
They slept the way tired children do: deeply and quietly.
Their two small breaths were the only sound left.
Bluey and Muffin slept on, cosy and warm and ready for tomorrow.

<LINE>The moon was up when Gabby found a sparkly quilt near the playroom rug.</LINE>
<LINE>Gabby turned the lamp down low and climbed into bed.</LINE>
<LINE>Gabby put on soft pyjamas and sat down near the playroom rug.</LINE>
<LINE>Gabby stacked the pillows neatly and gave them a pat.</LINE>
<LINE>Gabby put the slippers by the bed and climbed under the quilt.</LINE>
<LINE>A plane blinked quietly across the top of the sky.</LINE>
<LINE>All the little lights in the street had gone out.</LINE>
<LINE>MerCat was still wide awake when the moon was up.</LINE>
<LINE>Gabby heard MerCat move restlessly near the playroom rug.</LINE>
<LINE>Gabby offered to sit there as long as it took.</LINE>
<LINE>They rearranged the pillows until it felt comfortable.</LINE>
<LINE>Gabby fetched a glass of water for MerCat.</LINE>
<LINE>Gabby sat with MerCat until the wriggling stopped.</LINE>
<LINE>Gabby showed MerCat how to snuggle down into the warm spot.</LINE>
<LINE>MerCat whispered thank you and closed their eyes.</LINE>
<LINE>Everything was steady and calm and kind.</LINE>
<LINE>The room felt softer once the problem was solved.</LINE>
<LINE>Nothing stirred except the curtain and the clock.</LINE>
<LINE>Somewhere a clock ticked slowly, on and on.</LINE>
<LINE>The quilt was warm and the pillow was soft.</LINE>
<LINE>And every star watched over them until morning.</LINE>
<LINE>MerCat mumbled something happy and slept on.</LINE>
<LINE>Gabby and MerCat slept on, snug and warm near the playroom rug.</LINE>
<END>

lines: The moon was up when Gabby found a fluffy pillow near the playroom rug.
Gabby turned the pillow over to the cool side and sighed.
Gabby drank the last of the warm milk and yawned.
Gabby put on soft pyjamas and sat down near the playroom rug.
Gabby rolled over once, then found the very best spot.
The curtains were open just enough for the moonlight.
The rooftops were dark and the chimneys stood still.
One warm blanket, and two friends who both wanted it.
There was one soft bed, but two sleepy friends who wanted it.
Gabby offered to stay up a little longer.
Gabby wound the music box and shared the quiet tune.
They made a warm pocket for four cold feet.
Gabby moved over so there was room for both.
Gabby saved the softest corner for Pandy Paws.
Sharing turned out to be easy and warm.
Kindness was easy when there was plenty to go round.
Pandy Paws felt happy and snug again after all.
The moon kept a soft, silver watch through the window.
Their eyelids grew heavy, and their arms felt warm and relaxed.
Nothing moved now except the gentle moon.
Both of them were cosy, and both were sound asleep.
Dreams arrived without any fuss at all.
Gabby and Pandy Paws slept on, snug and warm near the playroom rug.

One set the knitted quilt where it would be handy, then stretched out.
One shooed the last thoughts away and closed the curtains.
One put the slippers by the bed and climbed under the quilt.
The rooftops were dark and the chimneys stood still.
Even the dust in the lamplight seemed to drift down very slowly.
It was very dark by the playroom rug in the middle of the night.
A soft creak in the dark made One sit quietly and listen.
One said they were glad to help a friend.
At the last step, the shadow was only a pile of clothes.
One checked the hallway twice and felt quite brave.
One crept past the creaky floorboard and waved.
One peered round the playroom rug and found nothing there.
Three let out a happy little breath at last.
The hallway felt just like any other room.
The house was quiet, and nothing was frightening.
Every single sound settled down and went to sleep.
The quilt was warm and the pillow was soft.
The house settled into its quiet, sleepy self.
Sleep came quietly, like a soft blanket over them.
One drifted into a lovely dream about the day.
One and Three counted back from ten and fell asleep.

lines: One found a fluffy pillow near the playroom rug and counted one, two, three.
One tidied the toys away and put them all to bed.
One rubbed tired eyes and looked around the quiet playroom rug.
One shook out the pillow and punched it into shape.
One tucked the teddy under one arm and got comfortable.
A soft hush fell over the street and the roofs.
The curtains moved a little, and the shadows danced quietly.
A shape in the corner looked taller than it should.
A soft creak in the dark made One sit quietly and listen.
One offered to sit there as long as it took.
One checked the hallway twice and felt quite brave.
They walked the hallway slowly and found it ordinary.
Five took a step and found it was not scary.
One said the dark was just the dark, that is all.
There was nothing left to be scared of now.
One felt calm, and rather pleased.
The night felt small and safe and friendly.
The dark was kind, and the blankets were heavy.
The room smelled faintly of lavender and soap.
The quilt was warm and the pillow was soft.
Nothing worried them, and nothing woke them.
And that is where the night left them: safe, warm, asleep.
One and Five counted back from ten and fell asleep.

lines: One found a bedtime rhyme near the playroom rug and counted one, two, three.
One yawned twice, stretched long, and settled right down.
One laid out the slippers side by side and stepped in.
One plumped the pillow twice and pulled up the sheet.
One shook out the pillow and punched it into shape.
A thin cloud slid across the moon and made the room dim.
A cool breeze tapped the window once, and then wandered off.
One wondered what that noise could possibly be.
A shape in the corner looked taller than it should.
One offered to stay up a little longer.
One took a slow breath and stepped slowly into the dark.
One held the little light up high and looked around.
Every shadow turned out to be something ordinary.
One peered round the playroom rug and found nothing there.
One was not scared of the dark any more.
Two let out a happy little breath at last.
The hallway felt just like any other room.
Everything was in its right place and felt just right.
Everything soft was close, and everything loud was far.
The world outside had gone completely still.
Their two small breaths were the only sound left.
One sank down into the deepest kind of sleepy.
One and Two counted back from ten and fell asleep.

One turned the pillow over to the cool side and sighed.
One set the knitted quilt where it would be handy, then stretched out.
One whispered goodnight to the moon through the glass.
The garden gate swung once and settled back with a click.
Everything outdoors had gone soft and grey and sleepy.
One warm blanket, and two friends who both wanted it.
There was one soft bed, but two sleepy friends who wanted it.
One whispered a plan and Three nodded slowly.
One shared the knitted quilt with Three and felt good.
They decided to share the quilt and the pillow both.
One tucked Three in first, then settled down too.
Both of them squeezed in and made it work.
The blanket felt warm because it was shared.
They both felt warm, and very, very sleepy.
Two friends, one quilt, and no cold corners.
It was the kind of quiet that meant a good sleep was coming.
The little lamp was turned down to the gentlest glow.
The lamp went dark and the room went softer still.
And every star watched over them until morning.
Three mumbled something happy and slept on.
One and Three counted back from ten and fell asleep.

One whispered goodnight to the moon through the glass.
One rolled over once, then found the very best spot.
One yawned twice, stretched long, and settled right down.
One hummed while getting ready and took the long way to the counting stair.
The clock in the hall ticked on, patient and slow.
Even the dust in the lamplight seemed to drift down very slowly.
There was one cosy spot, and it was already taken.
One saw Five hugging their knees in the dark.
One promised they would not go far.
They wrapped up together and shared the warm spot.
One shared the fluffy pillow with Five and felt good.
One made a nest with room enough for two.
They huddled up together and told jokes softly.

Five beamed and wriggled down happily.
Five felt happy and snug again after all.
The night wrapped the house up, warm and quiet.
Nothing stirred except the curtain and the clock.
The moon kept a soft, silver watch through the window.
Their breathing slowed to a soft, steady rhythm.
One slept deeply, all the way until morning.
One and Five counted back from ten and fell asleep.

One propped the pillow behind and sank down happily.
One straightened the quilt and smoothed it down flat.
One turned the lamp down low and climbed into bed.
Somewhere far off an owl called once, then went back to sleep.
The clock in the hall ticked on, patient and slow.
A shadow slid along the wall and disappeared.
One felt a small flutter in the tummy but stayed still.
One decided to help Two straight away.
Every shadow turned out to be something ordinary.
Two kept close and held on tight.
They listened hard and heard only the wind.
One said the dark was just the dark, that is all.
One felt proud, and very ready for sleep.
Two was not afraid of the dark at all now.
The house was quiet, and nothing was frightening.
The last light clicked off and the room went soft.
Nothing needed doing, and nothing needed saying.
The house settled into its quiet, sleepy self.
Two mumbled something happy and slept on.
And there they stayed, asleep and warm, until morning.
One and Two counted slowly down and drifted off.

lines: The moon was up, and One found a soft blanket near the counting stair.
One whispered goodnight to the toys on the shelf.
One set the soft blanket where it would be handy, then stretched out.
One put on soft pyjamas and sat down near the counting stair.
One shook out the pillow and punched it into shape.
The rooftops were dark and the chimneys stood still.
One star seemed to blink, as if it was getting sleepy too.
The hallway stretched away into the dark.
A shadow slid along the wall and disappeared.
One said two kind words and meant every one.
One quiet step, then another, and another after that.
They walked the hallway slowly and found it ordinary.
One took one more step and was not worried.
They listened hard and heard only the wind.
The hallway felt just like any other room.
Three was not afraid of the dark at all now.
Three felt brave too, and very sleepy.
Everything had that safe, tucked-in feeling.
Their eyelids grew heavy, and their arms felt warm and relaxed.
Somewhere a clock ticked slowly, on and on.
Slowly, quietly, the two of them drifted away.
One slept deeply, all the way until morning.
One and Three counted slowly down and drifted off.

lines: The moon was up, and One found a night light near the counting stair.
One laid out the slippers side by side and stepped in.
One checked that the little lamp was glowing just right.
One put away the day and hung up the busy thoughts.
One propped the pillow behind and sank down happily.
All the little lights in the street had gone out.
The curtains were open just enough for the moonlight.
It was very dark by the counting stair in the middle of the night.
A little shadow moved slowly across the dark counting stair.
One said they would not leave Five alone.
One peered round the counting stair and found nothing there.
They found the noise was only a curtain flapping.
One held the little light up high and looked around.
One checked the hallway twice and felt quite brave.
The dark turned friendly, and they walked home slowly, side by side.
One felt proud, and very ready for sleep.
Brave feelings lasted all the way back to bed.
The dark was soft, like a room with the lights down low.
The moon kept a soft, silver watch through the window.
Nothing needed doing, and nothing needed saying.
Five fell asleep with a tiny, contented smile.
One sank down into the deepest kind of sleepy.
One and Five counted slowly down and drifted off.

lines: The moon was up, and One found a star chart near the counting stair.
One turned the pillow over to the cool side and sighed.
One tucked the quilt in at the sides and yawned.
One folded the covers just so and made everything nice and neat.
One whispered goodnight to the moon through the glass.
The window glass had gone cool against the quiet night.
The stars came out one by one, like someone was switching them on.
One wondered what that noise could possibly be.
A shadow slid along the wall and disappeared.
One gave Two a look that said it would be fine.
One held the little light up high and looked around.
Two took a step and found it was not scary.
Two kept close and held on tight.
One crept past the creaky floorboard and waved.
They were not afraid of anything in the dark.
Two let out a happy little breath at last.
One felt calm, and rather pleased.
The dark wrapped around the quiet room like something warm.
Nothing moved now except the gentle moon.
The air smelled faintly of soap and warm blankets.
And that was the end: one more sleepy, happy night.
Morning was a long, long way off yet.
One and Two counted slowly down and drifted off.

One whispered goodnight to the toys on the shelf.
One folded the covers just so and made everything nice and neat.

One tucked the teddy under one arm and got comfortable.

One held the little light up high and looked around.

The lamp went dark and the room went softer still.
Nothing worried them, and nothing woke them.
And every star watched over them until morning.
One and Five counted slowly down and drifted off.

lines: The moon was up, and One found a soft blanket near the counting stair.
One rolled over once, then found the very best spot.
One brushed the crumbs off the sheet and climbed in.
One shook out the pillow and punched it into shape.
One put the slippers by the bed and climbed under the quilt.
The curtains were open just enough for the moonlight.
Somewhere in the garden a cricket began its slow song.
The story would not end the way One had planned.
The quilt would not sit straight no matter what.
One put a gentle arm around Two and smiled.
They took a short rest, then tried the whole thing again.
The next try was better than the last one.
One adjusted it carefully and stood back to look.
One steadied it carefully and tried one last time.
It was finished, and it was tidy, and it was time for sleep.
All that trying was the sleepiest part of the day.
It stayed put, right where it should be.
The quilt was warm and the pillow was soft.
It was the quietest part of the whole night.
Nothing moved now except the gentle moon.
Everything went soft and slow, and everyone was asleep.
Slowly, quietly, the two of them drifted away.
One and Two counted slowly down and drifted off.

lines: The moon was up, and One found a night light near the counting stair.
One drank some water, then lay down for the night.
One made a good nest by the counting stair with a night light.
One pulled the quilt up to the chin and sighed happily.
One wrapped up snugly and grinned at how soft the night light was.
Somewhere in the garden a cricket began its slow song.
The garden gate swung once and settled back with a click.
One wanted it to be perfect before sleeping.
One tried to think of the very best idea.
One whispered a plan and Three nodded slowly.
The next try was better than the last one.
One practised quietly until it felt easier.
It was not perfect the second time, but it was better.
They changed one small thing and gave it another go.
It worked, and they were both quietly proud.
It was finished, and it was tidy, and it was time for sleep.
It worked, and that was the end of the fuss.
Everything was in its right place and felt just right.
The pillows settled, and the quilt settled, and the room settled.
The house creaked once, the way houses do at night.
Three fell asleep with a tiny, contented smile.
And so the long, soft night began.
One and Three counted slowly down and drifted off.

<LINE>The moon was up when Amelia started the bedtime jobs near the living room rug.</LINE>
<LINE>Amelia drank some water, then lay down for the night.</LINE>
<LINE>Amelia stacked the pillows neatly and gave them a pat.</LINE>
<LINE>Amelia whispered goodnight to the toys on the shelf.</LINE>
<LINE>Amelia brushed the crumbs off the sheet and climbed in.</LINE>
<LINE>A cool breeze tapped the window once, and then wandered off.</LINE>
<LINE>One star seemed to blink, as if it was getting sleepy too.</LINE>
<LINE>Amelia could tell that Mrs. Rogers needed some company.</LINE>
<LINE>Amelia heard Mrs. Rogers move restlessly near the living room rug.</LINE>
<LINE>Amelia said they were glad to help a friend.</LINE>
<LINE>Amelia tucked the quilt round and left the lamp glowing.</LINE>
<LINE>Together they counted down from ten, very slowly.</LINE>
<LINE>They rearranged the pillows until it felt comfortable.</LINE>
<LINE>Amelia fetched the warm blanket and brought it over to Mrs. Rogers.</LINE>
<LINE>Amelia pulled the covers up again and smiled.</LINE>
<LINE>Being helpful had made the whole night gentler.</LINE>
<LINE>Amelia felt glad, and warm, and ready for bed.</LINE>
<LINE>The quilt was warm and the pillow was soft.</LINE>
<LINE>The lamp went dark and the room went softer still.</LINE>
<LINE>Everything soft was close, and everything loud was far.</LINE>
<LINE>Mrs. Rogers fell asleep with a tiny, contented smile.</LINE>
<LINE>And so the long, soft night began.</LINE>
<LINE>Amelia and Mrs. Rogers said goodnight and slept, warm and safe.</LINE>
<END>

lines: The moon was up when Amelia started the bedtime jobs near the living room rug.
Amelia whispered goodnight to the toys on the shelf.
Amelia drank the last of the warm milk and yawned.
Amelia hummed while getting ready and took the long way to the living room rug.
Amelia put on soft pyjamas and sat down near the living room rug.
A cool breeze tapped the window once, and then wandered off.
Everything outside was resting, from the trees to the stones.
Amelia heard a tiny sniffle from across the room.
Mr. Rogers was up and pacing quietly round the living room rug.
Amelia put a gentle arm around Mr. Rogers and smiled.
Together they counted down from ten, very slowly.
Amelia sat with Mr. Rogers until the wriggling stopped.
Amelia sang the quiet song twice more, softer each time.
Amelia fetched the hot water bottle and brought it over to Mr. Rogers.
The worrying feeling drifted off somewhere else.
Mr. Rogers whispered thank you and closed their eyes.
Amelia pulled the covers up again and smiled.
The last light clicked off and the room went soft.
The dark was kind, and the blankets were heavy.
The dark was soft, like a room with the lights down low.
Sleep came quietly, like a soft blanket over them.
The house kept them safe while they slept.
Amelia and Mr. Rogers said goodnight and slept, warm and safe.

Amelia tucked the teddy under one arm and got comfortable.
The rooftops were dark and the chimneys stood still.
The sky was wide and calm, like a big dark quilt.
Amelia heard a small, uncertain voice coming from the living room rug.
Amelia heard a tiny sniffle from across the room.
Amelia offered to help before Mrs. Rogers even asked.
Amelia showed Mrs. Rogers how to snuggle down into the warm spot.
Amelia tucked the quilt round and left the lamp glowing.

They built a little nest that felt exactly right.
Mrs. Rogers whispered thank you and closed their eyes.

Amelia pulled the covers up again and smiled.

Everything was still, and everything was well.
It was the quietest part of the whole night.
The dark kept them company, gentle and warm.
Amelia closed their eyes and floated off gently to sleep.
Amelia and Mrs. Rogers said goodnight and slept, warm and safe.

Amelia checked that the little lamp was glowing just right.
Amelia stacked the pillows neatly and gave them a pat.
Amelia tidied the toys away and put them all to bed.
Amelia kicked off the slippers and wiggled ten tired toes.

A cool breeze tapped the window once, and then wandered off.
Mr. Rogers could not seem to fall asleep, no matter how hard they tried.
Amelia heard Mr. Rogers move restlessly near the living room rug.
Amelia promised to check on them later.
Together they found the best place, then made it soft and warm.
Amelia fetched a glass of water for Mr. Rogers.
Amelia fetched the night light and brought it over to Mr. Rogers.
Amelia brought a small torch and checked the corners.

The little problem had completely gone away.
Amelia felt glad, and warm, and ready for bed.

Nothing moved now except the gentle moon.
The house breathed out and settled for the night.
Amelia drifted into a lovely dream about the day.
Dreams arrived without any fuss at all.
Amelia and Mr. Rogers said goodnight and slept, warm and safe.

lines: The moon was up when Amelia started the bedtime jobs near the living room rug.
Amelia rolled over once, then found the very best spot.
Amelia closed the little book and set it down gently.
Amelia turned the lamp down low and climbed into bed.

The house breathed out and settled for the night.
Mr. Rogers fell asleep with a tiny, contented smile.
And there they stayed, asleep and warm, until morning.
Amelia and Mr. Rogers said goodnight and slept, warm and safe.

<LINE>Junie found a stripy quilt near the hallway floor and decided to be very nice.</LINE>
<LINE>Junie let the busy day melt away and got completely comfy.</LINE>
<LINE>Junie tucked the quilt in at the sides and yawned.</LINE>
<LINE>Junie shooed the last thoughts away and closed the curtains.</LINE>
<LINE>Junie tidied the toys away and put them all to bed.</LINE>
<LINE>The moon was so round and bright that it lit up the whole room.</LINE>
<LINE>The garden gate swung once and settled back with a click.</LINE>
<LINE>Grace had nothing cosy to keep them warm.</LINE>
<LINE>Grace wanted a turn with the only warm thing.</LINE>
<LINE>Junie told Grace they were doing really well.</LINE>
<LINE>They huddled up together and told jokes softly.</LINE>
<LINE>Junie covered Grace with the warmer blanket.</LINE>
<LINE>Both of them squeezed in and made it work.</LINE>
<LINE>Junie tucked Grace in first, then settled down too.</LINE>
<LINE>The blanket felt warm because it was shared.</LINE>
<LINE>Kindness was easy when there was plenty to go round.</LINE>
<LINE>Sharing made the room feel warmer and kinder.</LINE>
<LINE>The dark was kind, and the blankets were heavy.</LINE>
<LINE>The night wrapped the house up, warm and quiet.</LINE>
<LINE>The last little sound faded out into the dark.</LINE>
<LINE>Nothing worried them, and nothing woke them.</LINE>
<LINE>Junie drifted into a lovely dream about the day.</LINE>
<LINE>Junie and Grace fell asleep, kind and happy and cosy.</LINE>
<END>

lines: Junie found a woolly jumper near the hallway floor and decided to be very nice.
Junie drank some water, then lay down for the night.
Junie shook out the pillow and punched it into shape.
Junie put the slippers by the bed and climbed under the quilt.
Junie tucked the quilt in at the sides and yawned.
Somewhere in the garden a cricket began its slow song.
A thin cloud slid across the moon and made the room dim.
Herb wanted a turn with the only warm thing.
Junie saw Herb hugging their knees in the dark.
Junie offered to sit there as long as it took.
Junie offered the best spot to Herb first.
Two friends, one blanket, and plenty of space for both.
Junie covered Herb with the warmer blanket.
They made room so both of them could lie down.
Kindness made even the dark room feel friendly.
Kindness was easy when there was plenty to go round.
They both felt warm, and very, very sleepy.
The last light clicked off and the room went soft.
The little lamp was turned down to the gentlest glow.
It was the kind of quiet that meant a good sleep was coming.
They slept the way tired children do: deeply and quietly.
The room breathed slowly in and out all night.
Junie and Herb fell asleep, kind and happy and cosy.

Junie plumped the pillow twice and pulled up the sheet.
Junie put away the day and hung up the busy thoughts.
The sky had that deep, velvety look it gets at night.

Lucille wanted something warm to hold before resting.

Junie offered the best spot to Lucille first.

The night lay over the whole house like a quilt.
The night held them gently, the way a quilt does.
Morning was a long, long way off yet.
Junie and Lucille fell asleep, kind and happy and cosy.
